claims.text: (CrFeTiTa)70W30 is a refractory high-entropy alloy suitable for consideration as an interlayer in a tungsten/copper-side fusion component.
Coating W particles with a nanoscale (CrFeTiTa)70W30 layer before embedding them in a Cu matrix will reduce phase separation during consolidation.
The high-entropy-alloy coating will reduce interfacial void formation during sintering.
The coating will improve bonding at W–Cu interfaces.
The coating will improve thermal transport relative to uncoated spark-plasma-sintered W–Cu.
The coating will preserve or improve mechanical durability under irradiation relative to uncoated spark-plasma-sintered W–Cu.
Conventionally fabricated W–Cu matrices, including those made by spark-plasma sintering, exhibit interfacial voids and phase separation.
The deposited high-entropy-alloy layer will act as a graded interface between W and Cu.
The graded interface will minimize interfacial-energy differences between W and Cu.
The graded interface will reduce thermal-expansion mismatch between W and Cu.
The interlayer will improve wettability at the W–Cu interface.
The interlayer will improve chemical compatibility at the W–Cu interface.
The graded interface will stabilize the W–Cu microstructure during irradiation.

Refractory (CrFeTiTa)70W30 and VFeTiTaW alloys have previously been prepared and evaluated for thermal and irradiation resistance as candidate interlayers between tungsten and CuCrZr-side fusion components.
The proposed W–Cu composite is intended to withstand thermal flux and irradiation associated with fusion-reactor service.
Consolidation will be performed by spark-plasma sintering below 1000 °C.
The optimal interlayer thickness and composition are undetermined.
The long-term microstructural and irradiation stability of the coated composite under fusion-reactor operating conditions is undetermined.
